# Model selection (corrective action CA3) {#sec-selection}

## Procedure {#sec-sel-procedure}

Model selection was adopted as corrective action CA3 on `{python} sel_date`, before the investigation into acceptance criteria set after the data were seen (INV-001) closed on `{python} INV["closed"]`. It replaced the analysis of every output, the refits of corrective action CA2 included. Each report with a response-surface design applies it to every output of the design, on all runs in which the output was measured. Where a design was augmented, the planned runs form the first block and the augmentation runs the second. The verification of the platform worst cases behind the intermediate acceptance criteria applies the same procedure (@sec-sel-verification). The process characterization master plan (PCMP-001) is not changed. Each report records the model selection as a discrepancy from its plan (@sec-impact). The procedure has four steps:

1. The scale. The output is raised to a power λ, and the full quadratic model is fitted to the result, with the block term where the runs form two blocks, over a range of powers [@boxcox1964]. A power of λ = 1 leaves the output on its raw scale, and λ = 0 is read as the natural logarithm. For each power the profile likelihood measures how well the model fits the transformed output with residuals that are normal and of equal spread. Its 95 % interval is the set of powers that the data do not reject at the 5 % level. The output is modelled on the log scale (λ = 0) where this interval contains 0 and excludes 1. Otherwise it is modelled on the raw scale (λ = 1). The rule chooses between these two scales only, and only an output whose results are all positive can take the log scale. Where the interval excludes both 0 and 1, the raw scale is kept. On all runs this applies to `{python} eb_phrase`. On its planned runs alone the interval of `{python} eb_attr` contains 0 and excludes 1, and the model selected there is on the log scale. The scale is chosen on the full quadratic before the search, so that the search compares every candidate on one scale. An output whose results the full quadratic reproduces exactly has no interval, because its profile likelihood is then unbounded, and no scale is chosen for it.
2. The search. Every submodel of the full quadratic model that respects strong hierarchy is fitted on that scale. Strong hierarchy allows an interaction only together with both of its main effects, and a squared term only together with its main effect. The block term is kept in every candidate. The candidate with the lowest AICc is selected (@sec-sel-search). Where the full quadratic reproduces every run exactly, AICc is not defined, and the output has no adequate model (step 3).
3. The check. The selected model is judged on its own scale against the model-adequacy criteria of the master plan, which require `{python} TESTS`. A selected model with no term has no model F-test and is judged by the other two tests. A model that reproduces every run exactly is not adequate. With no residual there is no pure error for the lack-of-fit test and no residual mean square for the model F-test, so the criteria cannot be applied, and its prediction interval would have zero width. Only the selected model is judged. If it fails, no other candidate takes its place. The selection used the same runs that the criteria then judge. A model chosen as the best of many candidates fits those runs better than a model fixed in advance, so the check of a selected model against the model-adequacy criteria is optimistic. @sec-sel-aug gives the one independent check that exists.
4. The offset. The scale-down offset of an output is taken on the scale of its model, with its `{python} f"{100 * ci_off:.0f}"` % confidence interval. For a raw-scale output it is the mean of the scale-down set-point runs minus the mean of the manufacturing-scale batches, and it is subtracted from a scale-down prediction. For a log-scale output it is the same difference of the mean logarithms, reported as a ratio of geometric means, and a scale-down prediction is divided by it. An output with no adequate model takes its offset on the scale chosen in step 1, or on the raw scale where no scale is chosen.

The check of a selected model against the model-adequacy criteria has three outcomes. A selected model with terms that passes is the predictive model of the output, and it sets the ranges of its step. A selected model with no term passes when it meets the lack-of-fit test and the limit on overfitting. It says that no effect of the parameters was detected within the range studied. It does not show that there is none. For a model of the mean alone on a single block, R² is zero and R² minus predicted R² depends on the number of runs only, `{python} f2(gap_mean_only(n_lo))` for `{python} n_lo` runs and `{python} f2(gap_mean_only(n_hi))` for `{python} n_hi`, so for such a model the check reduces to the lack-of-fit test. With `{python} df_pe` degrees of freedom for pure error, that test has little power, and such a model passes it almost always. An output whose selected model fails, or fits exactly, has no adequate model. It is judged on its measured results, as @sec-rule describes, and it sets no range.

## Why a log scale, and what it changes {#sec-sel-log}

Host cell protein in the Protein A pool shows what the log scale does. On the log scale the selected model has the form

$$\ln y = b_0 + b_1 x_1 + b_2 x_2 + \dots + \varepsilon$$

and, transformed back,

$$y = e^{b_0} \cdot e^{b_1 x_1} \cdot e^{b_2 x_2} \cdots e^{\varepsilon}$$

Here y is pool host cell protein in `{python} hcp_unit`, x₁, x₂ and so on are the parameters in coded units, from −1 at the low end of the range studied to +1 at the high end, and ε is the error of a single run. One coded unit is therefore half the range studied. A parameter that enters the model as a main effect alone multiplies the output by a fixed factor, $e^{b}$ per coded unit and $e^{2b}$ from the low to the high end of its range. The error multiplies it too, so the scatter in `{python} hcp_unit` grows with the level.

`{python} cap1(pname(HK[0], LD))` shows how this reads in real units. Its range studied is `{python} f"{pl_ld.prange[0]:g}"` to `{python} f"{pl_ld.prange[1]:g}"` `{python} pl_ld.unit`, so one coded unit is `{python} f"{half_ld:g}"` `{python} pl_ld.unit`. Its coefficient on the log scale is b = `{python} f3(b_ld)`. Pool host cell protein therefore rises by a factor of $e^{b}$ = `{python} f2(np.exp(b_ld))` for every `{python} f"{half_ld:g}"` `{python} pl_ld.unit` of `{python} pname(HK[0], LD)`, and by $e^{2b}$ = `{python} f2(fold_h[LD])` from `{python} f"{pl_ld.prange[0]:g}"` to `{python} f"{pl_ld.prange[1]:g}"` `{python} pl_ld.unit`. Across the range studied, the selected model multiplies pool host cell protein by a factor of `{python} fold_txt`, from the low to the high end of each parameter. A factor below one is a decrease. `{python} cap1(pname(HK[0], FL))` also has a squared term, so its factor depends on where along the range the change is made. From `{python} f"{pl_fl.prange[0]:g}"` to `{python} f"{fl_mid:g}"` `{python} pl_fl.unit` pool host cell protein changes by a factor of `{python} f2(fl_lo)`, and from `{python} f"{fl_mid:g}"` to `{python} f"{pl_fl.prange[1]:g}"` `{python} pl_fl.unit` by a factor of `{python} f2(fl_hi)`.

Two properties of the process and the method make host cell protein behave this way. A purification step removes a share of what is present, so a parameter changes the share that is removed, not a fixed amount. The precision of the host cell protein ELISA (`{python} elisa["id"]`) is a percentage of the level, `{python} f"{elisa['precision_pct']:g}"` %, so the scatter of the results grows with the level. Effects that multiply look like an interaction when they are added on the raw scale. On the raw scale the full quadratic model needs the interaction `{python} int_h_txt` (`{python} ptxt(p_int_raw)`). On the log scale the same interaction is not significant (`{python} ptxt(p_int_log)`), and the selected model has no interaction at all.

Least squares needs no assumption about the distribution of the residuals to estimate the coefficients. The t-tests, F-tests and prediction intervals built on it assume residuals that are independent and normally distributed, with mean zero and the same variance over the whole range studied. The residuals of the full quadratic model of pool host cell protein show how the raw scale departs from this. Its runs were split at the median of the predicted values, `{python} n_half_lo` runs in the lower half and `{python} n_half_hi` in the upper half. On the raw scale the standard deviation of the residuals is `{python} f"{sd_raw_lo:,.0f}"` `{python} hcp_unit` in the lower half of the predictions and `{python} f"{sd_raw_hi:,.0f}"` `{python} hcp_unit` in the upper half, `{python} f"{sd_raw_ratio:.2f}"` times as large. On the log scale the same split gives `{python} f"{sd_log_lo:.3f}"` and `{python} f"{sd_log_hi:.3f}"` in natural-log units, `{python} f"{sd_log_ratio:.2f}"` times as large. On the log scale, therefore, the spread no longer grows with the level. Two halves of this size cannot show on their own that the raw-scale spread differs, and the Box-Cox profile is the evidence for the scale. It puts λ at `{python} f2(bc_h["lambda"])`, with a 95 % interval from `{python} num_txt(bc_h["lo"], 2)` to `{python} num_txt(bc_h["hi"], 2)`. The interval contains 0 and excludes 1, so the data support the log scale and reject the raw scale. This evidence concerns the full quadratic model, on which the scale is chosen, and not the smaller model selected afterwards. A test can fail to reject the assumption of equal variance, but it cannot show that the assumption holds.

The log scale changes the following:

1. The criterion stays in its own unit, `{python} hcp_unit`, and the prediction limits are transformed back into it.
2. Effects are fold changes, as above.
3. The scale-down offset is a ratio of geometric means, `{python} f2(off_h["offset"])` for pool host cell protein with a `{python} f"{100 * off_h['ci']:.0f}"` % confidence interval from `{python} f2(off_h["lo"])` to `{python} f2(off_h["hi"])`, and a scale-down prediction is divided by it.
4. A prediction interval is calculated on the log scale and transformed back. It keeps its 95 % coverage, because the probability that ln y lies between two values is the probability that y lies between their antilogs.
5. The interval is asymmetric, further above the predicted value than below it. At the least favourable combination of the NOR (`{python} wc_h_txt`), the model predicts ln y = `{python} f3(ln_w)` in the scale-down model. The 95 % prediction interval of a single batch is two-sided. On the log scale it is the prediction ± t·s·√(1 + h), where t = `{python} f3(t_w)` is the `{python} pct_t`th percentile of the t distribution with `{python} df_w` degrees of freedom, s = `{python} f3(s_w)` is the residual standard deviation on the log scale, and h = `{python} f3(h_w)` is the leverage of this combination. This gives `{python} f3(ln_w)` ± `{python} f3(half_w)`. Transformed back, the interval runs from `{python} f"{sd_lo_w:,.0f}"` to `{python} f"{sd_hi_w:,.0f}"` `{python} hcp_unit` around a median of `{python} f"{sd_med_w:,.0f}"` `{python} hcp_unit` in the scale-down model. Divided by the scale-down offset of `{python} f2(off_h["offset"])`, it runs from `{python} f"{wc_h['pi_low']:,.0f}"` to `{python} f"{wc_h['pi_high']:,.0f}"` `{python} hcp_unit` around a median of `{python} f"{wc_h['predicted']:,.0f}"` `{python} hcp_unit` at manufacturing scale, `{python} f"{wc_h['predicted'] - wc_h['pi_low']:,.0f}"` below and `{python} f"{wc_h['pi_high'] - wc_h['predicted']:,.0f}"` above. The conclusion over the NOR uses this two-sided interval. The verification of the platform worst cases uses the one-sided `{python} vb_pct` % bound instead (@sec-sel-verification).
6. The predicted value is the median of the output, its geometric mean, not its arithmetic mean. The upper prediction limit, which is judged against an upper criterion, is not affected by that.
7. Near an upper criterion, where the level is high, a raw-scale model pools one residual standard deviation over all levels and so understates the scatter, which the log-scale interval does not.

In the reports, `{python} n_log_sel` of the `{python} n_models` outputs with a criterion are modelled on the log scale. They are `{python} log_sel_phrase`.

## How the model is searched {#sec-sel-search}

The goal of the search is the model with the lowest AICc among all hierarchical submodels of the full quadratic. AICc estimates how well a model would predict new runs [@hurvich1989; @burnham2002]. It adds a fit term to a penalty. The fit term is n·ln(SSE/n), where n is the number of runs and SSE the residual sum of squares, and it falls as the fit improves. The penalty is 2K, where K counts the estimated quantities, the coefficients and the residual variance, plus a correction for small samples, 2K(K + 1)/(n − K − 1). A constant that is the same for every candidate is left out. A term is therefore kept only where it lowers the fit term by more than it raises the penalty. AICc is Akaike's criterion, AIC, with that correction. The correction raises the penalty when the runs are few for the number of terms, as in these designs, so that the criterion does not favour models with too many terms. For the full quadratic model on `{python} n4` runs, K is `{python} K_full` (`{python} k4` coefficients and the residual variance), so the penalty is `{python} aic_pen` and the correction adds `{python} f"{aicc_corr:.1f}"` to it.

Pool host cell protein in the Protein A pool shows the trade. On the log scale the fit term is `{python} num_txt(AP_f["fit"])` for the full quadratic model and `{python} num_txt(AP_s["fit"])` for the selected model. The selected model has `{python} len(fh["names"])` terms, so K is `{python} AP_s["K"]`, its penalty is `{python} AP_s["pen"]` and its correction `{python} f"{AP_s['corr']:.1f}"`. The full quadratic fits better by `{python} f"{d_fit:.1f}"`, but its penalty is larger by `{python} f"{d_pen:.1f}"`, so the selected model has the lower AICc, by `{python} f"{d_pen - d_fit:.1f}"`.

The search fits every candidate, `{python} f"{n_cand[4]:,}"` for a design with four factors, `{python} n_cand[3]` for three and `{python} n_cand[2]` for two, the model of the mean included. It takes the candidate with the lowest AICc. The candidates are listed in a fixed order, from the fewest main effects upward, and a tie goes to the first. A stepwise search, by contrast, adds or removes one term at a time and stops when no single change lowers AICc. It therefore stops where only a combination of changes would lower AICc further.

On this campaign's data the two searches were compared for `{python} n_cmp` outputs with a criterion. The output that fits exactly has no AICc and is left out. A backward stepwise search from the full quadratic would have stopped at a model with a higher AICc than the best candidate for `{python} n_bw` of them, a forward search from the mean for `{python} n_fw`, and one or the other for `{python} n_either`. For `{python} attr_prose(EXK[1], EXK[0])` `{python} at_step(EXK[0])`, for example, the exhaustive search selects `{python} int(ex.n_terms)` terms with an AICc of `{python} num_txt(ex.aicc)`. A backward search stops at `{python} int(ex.backward_terms)` terms (`{python} num_txt(ex.backward_aicc)`) and a forward search at `{python} int(ex.forward_terms)` terms (`{python} num_txt(ex.forward_aicc)`).

The backward elimination of corrective action CA2 differed from this search in three ways. It was stepwise. It decided by the p-value of each term. That p-value compares the model with and without the term, but it does not weigh the fit against the number of terms, and it cannot compare models that are not nested. It also worked on the raw scale only.

## Verification of the platform worst cases {#sec-sel-verification}

The process characterization master plan (PCMP-001) Version 2.0 derives the intermediate acceptance criteria a priori. Each drug substance criterion is carried back through the platform worst case of every downstream step, its lowest clearance fold or its largest increase, and each platform worst case is the result of a single run. The verification of these worst cases uses the same model selection, on the planned runs of each downstream step. For each worst case it predicts the output of the step at every combination of NOR low, set-point and NOR high of the NOR as characterized. At each combination it also takes the one-sided `{python} vb_pct` % prediction bound of a single batch, on the scale of the model and transformed back. Both are converted into a clearance fold or an increase, and the least favourable value over the combinations is the bound of the step.

Where the predicted value of a step is worse than the platform worst case, the bound replaces the platform value, and the criteria upstream of the step tighten. Where the bound itself is better than the platform worst case, on a selected model that meets the model-adequacy criteria (`{python} TESTS`), the bound replaces the platform value, and the criteria upstream widen. Otherwise the platform value stays. Both directions use the one-sided `{python} vb_pct` % prediction bound of a single batch, because every output is judged per batch and the platform worst case that the bound replaces was a single run. A bound from a tolerance interval covers a stated share of all batches with a stated confidence, and it is wider. The bound is pointwise at each combination, not simultaneous over them.

The platform worst cases of the low-pH hold are increases over a hold of `{python} plat_hold` min. The A-Mab value is the increase within the NOR as characterized, which allows a hold of at most `{python} nor_hold_max` min. At low pH the antibody forms aggregate, and the aggregate grows with the time at that pH. At the edges of the range studied, which include a hold of `{python} plat_hold` min, A-Mab adds up to `{python} f2(agg_edge)` percentage points of aggregate, more than the platform value of `{python} f2(agg_plat)`. Its single-batch bound of `{python} f3(agg_bound)` within the NOR as characterized is smaller than the platform value because that NOR ends at a shorter hold. The selected model of aggregate at low-pH viral inactivation has terms in `{python} fva_terms` only, and none in `{python} pname(VI, "ph")`. The NOR in force ends at the same longest `{python} pname(VI, "hold_time")`, `{python} f"{hold_p.nor[1]:g}"` `{python} hold_p.unit`, and the same highest `{python} pname(VI, "temperature")`, `{python} f"{temp_p.nor[1]:g}"` `{python} temp_p.unit`, as the NOR as characterized. The bound over the NOR as characterized therefore also covers the NOR in force. For acidic variants the model at low pH fits exactly and is not adequate, so its bound replaces no platform value (@sec-sel-exact). @sec-impact-criteria gives the criteria that the bounds of the selected models changed, and the risk of each change.

## What model selection changed {#sec-sel-changed}

Model selection gives an adequate model for `{python} n_sel_ok` of the `{python} n_models` outputs with a criterion. Every output whose full quadratic model met all three tests has an adequate selected model. Of the `{python} n_fail` outputs whose full quadratic model failed, `{python} n_fail_ok` have an adequate selected model and `{python} len(none_fail)` have none. The output whose full quadratic model fits exactly, `{python} exf_phrase`, has none either. @tbl-selected gives the verdict for every selected model, and @tbl-impact gives the model each report uses.

```{python}
#| output: asis
T.frame(sv_tbl, "Selected model of every response-surface output with a criterion against the model-adequacy criteria of PCMP-001.",
        "tbl-selected", merge=["Step"], header=sv_head, align=sv_align, notes=sv_notes, notes_per_row=True,
        size="footnotesize", landscape=True).show()
```

### The augmentations {#sec-sel-aug}

The three models that the augmentations were made for meet the model-adequacy criteria (`{python} TESTS`) on the planned runs alone once they are selected. They are the models of high mannose and acidic variants at the production bioreactor and of host cell protein at anion exchange. The augmentations were therefore not needed to pass these criteria. They were decided on `{python} decided` under the model of the plan, the full quadratic, which failed the limit on overfitting on the planned runs. Both started before model selection was adopted on `{python} sel_date`. The anion exchange runs were still under way on that date, as were the production bioreactor runs, and both were completed.

The augmentations were sized so that the full quadratic model with a block term would meet the lack-of-fit test and the limit on overfitting on all runs. On all runs it meets both for acidic variants and for host cell protein at anion exchange, with R² minus predicted R² of `{python} f2(FA[AV]["gap"])` and `{python} f2(FA[HCP]["gap"])`. For high mannose it does not, because R² minus predicted R² is `{python} f2(FA[HM]["gap"])` against the limit of `{python} gap_max_s`. Its lack-of-fit test is passed (`{python} ptxt(FA[HM]["p_lof"])`).

@tbl-sharpen gives the three selected models on the planned runs and on all runs, with the statistics of the model-adequacy criteria. Each meets the criteria on both sets of runs. For high mannose, `{python} len(AUG[HM]["dropped"])` terms of the model selected on the planned runs are not in the model selected on all runs. These are `{python} hm_dropped`. On all runs the selected model of high mannose is on the log scale and has `{python} len(AUG[HM]["sel_a"]["names"])` terms (`{python} hm_all`). The scale changed with the second block as well, so part of the change in terms may come from the scale. For acidic variants every term of the model selected on the planned runs is kept on all runs, and the second block resolves `{python} len(AUG[AV]["added"])` further terms (`{python} av_added`). For host cell protein at anion exchange the selected model is the same on both sets of runs. It has the main effects of `{python} hcp_terms`, on the log scale.

```{python}
#| output: asis
T.frame(sh_tbl, "Selected models of the outputs that the augmentations were made for, on the planned runs and on all runs.",
        "tbl-sharpen", merge=["Step", "Attribute"], header=sh_head, align=sh_align, notes=sh_notes,
        notes_per_row=True, size="footnotesize").show()
```

@tbl-aug-check tests each model selected on the planned runs of the two augmented steps against the augmentation runs, which it has not seen. If a model is right, each new run falls inside its 95 % prediction interval with a probability of `{python} f2(cover)`, and its prediction error is close to its own residual standard deviation. The effectiveness check of @sec-effectiveness judges such a count by a one-sided binomial test at the `{python} f"{eff_alpha:g}"` level. With `{python} int(hm_c.n_new)` new runs, that test rejects a model with fewer than `{python} int(hm_c.k_min)` inside. Only `{python} int(hm_c.inside_pi)` of the `{python} int(hm_c.n_new)` new runs fall inside the interval for high mannose and `{python} int(agg_c.inside_pi)` for aggregates at the production bioreactor, and the test rejects both models (`{python} ptxt(hm_c.p_binom)` and `{python} ptxt(agg_c.p_binom)`). Their prediction error is `{python} f"{hm_c.ratio:.1f}"` and `{python} f"{agg_c.ratio:.1f}"` times the residual standard deviation of the model. For the other outputs the ratio is at most `{python} f"{others_ratio:.1f}"`, and every count passes the test.

```{python}
#| output: asis
T.frame(apc_tbl, "Prediction of the augmentation runs by the models selected on the planned runs.", "tbl-aug-check",
        merge=["Step"], header=apc_head, align=apc_align, notes=apc_notes, notes_per_row=True,
        size="footnotesize").show()
```

The block term of the models on all runs tests for a constant shift between the planned and the augmentation runs. Its p-values give no evidence of one, the smallest being `{python} f"{block_p_min:.3f}"`. That is not evidence that nothing changed between the two campaigns. The planned production bioreactor runs ended on `{python} bio_rsm_end` and the augmentation began on `{python} aug_start["bioreactor"]`. A change in an effect would show at the corners that the augmentation repeats, runs `{python} bio_corner_runs` at the production bioreactor, as unequal differences between the repeated and the planned results. For high mannose these differences vary no more than run-to-run variation explains (`{python} ptxt(CC[HM]["p"])`). For aggregates they vary more, though not significantly at the `{python} f"{100 * eff_a:g}"` % level (`{python} ptxt(CC[AGG]["p"])`). With only `{python} CC[AGG]["n"]` pairs the comparison has little power, so a change in the aggregate effects between the campaigns cannot be excluded.

On all runs, high mannose loses the interactions `{python} hm_int_txt` that the planned runs suggested. Aggregates lose the terms `{python} agg_drop_txt` and gain a curvature in `{python} agg_add_txt.replace("²", "")`. The reports use the models of all runs. For acidic variants the model selected on the planned runs predicts every new run within its interval, and the model of all runs adds the terms that the second block resolves.

### Outputs with no adequate model {#sec-sel-none}

After selection, `{python} n_none_sel` outputs have no adequate model. They are `{python} none_sel_phrase`. Each is judged on its measured results (@sec-rule). @tbl-measured gives each criterion, the number of results, the most adverse measured result and the margin between them. Every measured result meets its criterion. None of these outputs sets a range.

```{python}
#| output: asis
T.frame(mr_tbl, "Outputs with no adequate model, judged on their measured results.", "tbl-measured",
        merge=["Step"], header=mr_head, align=mr_align, notes=mr_notes, notes_per_row=True, size="footnotesize").show()
```

The fragment models `{python} none_frag_txt` had no adequate refit under corrective action CA2 either. XMuLV clearance at virus filtration is the one output for which model selection and the refit by backward elimination disagree on whether an adequate model exists. The refit had reduced it to its mean, which meets the lack-of-fit test and the limit on overfitting. Model selection keeps a term in `{python} vf_terms`, because that model has the lower AICc (`{python} num_txt(fv["aicc"])` against `{python} num_txt(aicc_mean_vf)` for the mean alone). Only the selected model is judged. Its model F-test is not significant (`{python} ptxt(fv["p"])`), and its R² minus predicted R² of `{python} f2(fv["gap"])` exceeds the limit of `{python} gap_max_s`. XMuLV clearance at virus filtration is therefore judged on its measured results. The two models differ by `{python} f"{d_aicc_vf:.1f}"` in AICc. Models within two units of each other have about equal support [@burnham2002], so the outcome for this output rests on a small difference.

### An output that fits exactly {#sec-sel-exact}

`{python} cap1(attr_prose(EXF[1], EXF[0]))` `{python} at_step(EXF[0])` have results with no scatter. Every run at the same `{python} pname(VI, "hold_time")` returned the same value, in the screening and the response-surface designs alike, the replicated centre points included. The full quadratic model, which contains `{python} pname(VI, "hold_time")` and its square, therefore reproduces every run exactly, and so does the model with `{python} pname(VI, "hold_time")` alone. With no residual there is no pure error for the lack-of-fit test and no residual mean square for the model F-test, so the model-adequacy criteria cannot be applied. A prediction interval would have zero width. The Box-Cox profile likelihood is unbounded, so no scale is chosen and no interval is reported. The output therefore has no adequate model, and it is judged on its measured results (@tbl-measured). Its bound cannot replace a platform value in the verification of the platform worst cases (@sec-sel-verification). The upper limit of acidic variants at the production bioreactor therefore stays at its a priori value of `{python} T.num(av_in)` %.

### Outputs with no detected effect

The selected models of `{python} n_zero_sel` outputs have no term. They are `{python} zero_sel_phrase`. No effect of the parameters on them was detected within the ranges studied. The model is their mean, with the block term where the design has two blocks.

# Impact assessment {#sec-impact}

Model selection, corrective action CA3, replaces the full quadratic model of every output with a criterion in the report of its step. @tbl-impact lists the outputs by report. For each output it gives the remedy that the remedy rule gave a full quadratic model that failed the model-adequacy criteria (`{python} TESTS`), the model that the report uses after model selection, and the discrepancies from the plan that the report records.

```{python}
#| output: asis
T.frame(imp_df, "Response-surface outputs with a criterion by report, with the remedy and the model the report uses.",
        "tbl-impact", merge=["Report", "Discrepancies"], header=imp_head, align=imp_align, notes=imp_notes,
        notes_per_row=True, size="footnotesize").show()
```

Each report records the augmentation and the model selection as discrepancies from its plan, identified as plan discrepancies (PD). A discrepancy from the plan records work or an analysis that the approved plan did not foresee. A deviation records a departure from a procedure or a GMP requirement. No procedure and no GMP requirement was departed from, so neither is recorded as a deviation. The production bioreactor report (`{python} rep["bioreactor"]`) records the production bioreactor augmentation as `{python} pd_id["bioreactor"]`, and the anion exchange report (`{python} rep["aex"]`) records the anion exchange augmentation as `{python} pd_id["aex"]`. Each of the `{python} n_steps` reports with a response-surface design records the model selection (`{python} sel_pd_txt`). The process characterization master plan (PCMP-001) and the step plans are not amended.

## Acceptance criteria {#sec-impact-criteria}

Model selection was adopted on `{python} sel_date`, before the investigation into acceptance criteria set after the data were seen (INV-001) closed on `{python} INV["closed"]` and fixed the intermediate acceptance criteria. The verification of the platform worst cases behind the criteria in force therefore used the selected models of the planned runs (@sec-sel-verification). In force, the verification widened `{python} n_w_in` criteria by replacing a platform worst case with the one-sided `{python} vb_pct` % prediction bound of a single A-Mab batch, the single-batch bound, for `{python} w_in_txt`, and the criterion for `{python} w_in_tt_txt` was also tightened by another downstream step. The same verification on the full quadratic models, the analysis the plans prescribed, gives different values for `{python} n_cd` criteria. Against them, model selection made `{python} n_wider` criteria wider, by `{python} pct_txt`, and kept `{python} len(kept)` at its a priori value. @tbl-criteria-ca3 lists them, with the downstream worst cases whose values differ between the two verifications.

```{python}
#| output: asis
T.CTable(header=crit_head, body=crit_body, caption="Intermediate acceptance criteria that differ between the verification on the full quadratic models and on the selected models.",
         label="tbl-criteria-ca3", align=crit_align, notes=crit_notes, notes_per_row=True, size="footnotesize").show()
```

The differences between the criteria from the two verifications come from changes at `{python} n_change_steps` downstream steps:

1. Anion exchange. The full quadratic model of host cell protein fails the limit on overfitting, so its single-batch bound of `{python} b_aex_f` cannot widen a criterion, and the platform worst-case clearance fold of `{python} p_aex` enters the derivation. The selected model meets the model-adequacy criteria, and its bound of `{python} b_aex_s` replaces the platform fold. The host cell protein criteria `{python} hcp_crit_txt` therefore widen, because both lie upstream of anion exchange.
2. Cation exchange. The selected model of aggregate is on the log scale with `{python} n_terms_cxa` terms, and it gives a different prediction and a different single-batch bound from the full quadratic model. The predicted aggregate fold is worse than the platform fold on both models, so the bound replaces it on both. It tightens the aggregate criteria `{python} agg_crit_txt`, which lie upstream of cation exchange, by a different amount on each model. For host cell protein the predicted fold meets the platform fold of `{python} p_cexh` on both models and its single-batch bound does not, so the platform fold stays on both, and no criterion moves because of host cell protein at cation exchange.
3. Low-pH viral inactivation. For aggregate, the single-batch bound of the increase is better than the platform value on both models, differs slightly between them, and enters the production bioreactor criterion (@sec-sel-verification gives why it is smaller than the platform value). For acidic variants, the full quadratic model reproduces every run exactly. The verification on the full quadratic models found that none of its tests failed and took its bound of `{python} g3(av_bound)` percentage points, which would have widened the upper limit of acidic variants at the production bioreactor to `{python} T.num(av_full)` %. Model selection does not accept an exact fit as adequate (@sec-sel-exact). The platform value of `{python} f2(av_plat)` therefore stays, and the upper limit keeps its a priori value of `{python} T.num(av_apriori)` %.

Each widening rests on the one-sided `{python} vb_pct` % prediction bound of a single batch at the least favourable combination of the NOR as characterized, from a selected model that meets the model-adequacy criteria. A check of a selected model against these criteria is optimistic (@sec-sel-procedure), so @tbl-ca3-sensitivity shows what depends on the criteria that model selection moved. Judged against the criteria that the full quadratic models would have given, no output changes its conclusion over the NOR in force. One proven acceptable range moves. For host cell protein in the Protein A pool, the lower end of the `{python} pname(HK[0], PF)` range moves from `{python} f"{par_in[PF][0]:.2f}"` to `{python} f"{par_wo[PF][0]:.2f}"`, and both lie below the NOR of `{python} f"{pf_nor[0]:g}"` to `{python} f"{pf_nor[1]:g}"`.

Two qualifications of a scale-down model do depend on the wider criteria. A scale-down model is qualified for an output when its conclusion over the NOR is the same with the offset at either end of its `{python} f"{100 * ci_off:.0f}"` % confidence interval (PCMP-001 §7.1). Against the criteria without model selection, the scale-down model would not be qualified for host cell protein in the Protein A pool or at cation exchange. In both cases the low end of the offset interval decides. In the Protein A pool, with the offset at the low end of its interval, a ratio of `{python} f2(QD[HK]["off"]["lo"])`, the upper limit of the two-sided 95 % prediction interval of a single batch over the NOR, at manufacturing scale, is `{python} f"{QD[HK]['lim_lo']:,.0f}"` `{python} QD[HK]["unit"]`. That is above the criterion of `{python} f"{QD[HK]['crit_wo']:,.0f}"` `{python} QD[HK]["unit"]` that the full quadratic models give, and below the criterion in force of `{python} f"{QD[HK]['crit_in']:,.0f}"` `{python} QD[HK]["unit"]`. At cation exchange, with the offset at `{python} f2(QD[CXH]["off"]["lo"])`, the same limit is `{python} f"{QD[CXH]['lim_lo']:,.0f}"` `{python} QD[CXH]["unit"]`, against `{python} f"{QD[CXH]['crit_wo']:,.0f}"` `{python} QD[CXH]["unit"]` without model selection and `{python} f"{QD[CXH]['crit_in']:,.0f}"` `{python} QD[CXH]["unit"]` in force. These two qualifications rest on the criteria that model selection widened.

The wider criteria concern host cell protein and aggregates, which are attributes of the drug substance specification, with limits of `{python} join_and(f"{v:g} {u} {CQA_PL[c]}" for c, (v, u) in ds_by_cqa.items() if c in risk_cqas)`. A step output at its criterion still gives a drug substance within its limit, as long as each downstream step clears at least the value that the derivation uses. For host cell protein these are a fold of `{python} p_cexh` at cation exchange, the platform worst case, and `{python} b_aex_s` at anion exchange, its single-batch bound. For aggregates they are a fold of `{python} g3(cexa_fold_in)` at cation exchange and an increase of `{python} g3(via_add_in)` percentage points at low-pH viral inactivation, both single-batch bounds. The integrated process model simulates batches through every step of the train in sequence, from the step models with their run-to-run variation. Each process parameter of each batch is drawn from a normal distribution centred on its set-point, with a standard deviation of one sixth of the width of its NOR in force (PCMP-001 §6.4 and §6.5). None of its `{python} f"{n_mc_poos:,}"` simulated batches gives an out-of-specification drug substance for either attribute. With no failure in `{python} f"{n_mc_poos:,}"` batches, the one-sided 95 % upper bound on the rate of failure is `{python} f"{100 * oos_ub:.2f}"` %.

```{python}
#| output: asis
T.frame(sens_tbl, "What depends on the criteria that model selection moved.", "tbl-ca3-sensitivity",
        header=sens_head, align=sens_align, notes=sens_notes, notes_per_row=True, size="footnotesize").show()
```

The augmentation runs moved no criterion. Both augmentations ended after INV-001 closed, on `{python} aug_end_txt`, and the verification uses only the planned runs of each step. Repeated on all runs of anion exchange, the verification gives the same bound for host cell protein, `{python} f"{b_aex_all:.3g}"`, so the augmentation runs would not have moved the criteria either.

## Conclusions over the NOR {#sec-impact-nor}

The conclusion over the NOR of an output, whether it meets its criterion at every combination of NOR low, set-point and NOR high, does not depend on the choice between the full quadratic model of the planned runs and the model that the report uses. For every output with a criterion the two give the same conclusion, at the NOR as characterized and at the NOR in force. Two of these conclusions are not met on either model, and both rested on full quadratic models that fail the limit on overfitting:

1. XMuLV clearance at low-pH viral inactivation is judged on the mean LRF at the least favourable combination of NOR low, set-point and NOR high, because viral clearance is validated at worst-case conditions (PCMP-001 §6.4). The criterion is the platform claim of the step, `{python} f"{claim6:g}"` log10. The claims of the three viral clearance steps add up to `{python} f"{vcum.claimed_sum:g}"` log10, against a cumulative requirement of `{python} f"{vcum.required:g}"` log10. The selected model has the main effects of `{python} fit6_terms` only. On it, the lowest mean LRF within the NOR as characterized is `{python} f2(y6.min())`, at `{python} worst6`, so the step claim is not met. The full quadratic model gives a lowest mean of `{python} f2(y6f.min())` and the same conclusion. The low-pH viral inactivation report (`{python} rep[vk]`) moves the NOR of `{python} moved6_txt`, and it states the conclusion over the NOR in force.
2. Acidic variants at the production bioreactor are judged on the 95 % prediction interval of a single batch at every combination of NOR low, set-point and NOR high. The lower limit of the criterion is `{python} f"{av_floor:g}"` %, the lower limit of the drug substance specification carried to the step unchanged. In the selected model acidic variants fall as `{python} pname(bk, "pH")` rises, as in the model of the A-Mab case study [@amab2009, Table 3.16]. The least favourable combination therefore lies at the NOR high of `{python} pname(bk, "pH")`. On the selected model of all runs, the lower prediction limit at `{python} worst_b` is `{python} f"{av_lo:.1f}"` % at manufacturing scale, so the criterion is not met. The predicted median at the same settings is `{python} f"{av_med:.1f}"` %, `{python} av_med_word` the criterion. On the full quadratic model of the planned runs the lower prediction limit at the same settings is `{python} f"{avc_full['pi_low']:.1f}"` %, and the criterion is not met either. The production bioreactor report (`{python} rep[bk]`) states how this result is handled.

`{python} cap1(none_sel_phrase)` have no adequate model and are judged on their measured results (@tbl-measured).

## Other documents

The other documents of the package are affected as follows:

1. INV-001, the investigation into acceptance criteria set after the data were seen, is not reopened. Its comparison of the Version 1.0 and Version 2.0 criteria uses the models that Version 1.0 fitted, so that it shows what the change of criteria moved.
2. The process characterization master plan (PCMP-001 §7.2) allows a failing model to be refitted, or not used to set a range. The augmentation is the rule of this investigation. The master plan is not changed for model selection, which each report records as a discrepancy from its plan.
3. The process characterization master report (PCMR-001) consolidates the conclusions of the step reports after the remedies and the model selection.

The investigation has no product impact. No batch was dispositioned on these models, and the Version 1.0 documents were on hold for BLA use.

# Corrective and preventive actions {#sec-capa}

@tbl-capa lists the corrective and preventive actions. Model selection, corrective action CA3, replaced in the reports the refits by backward elimination of corrective action CA2. Corrective action CA1, the augmentation of the designs that the remedy rule names, has two parts. The augmentation runs of CA1 were complete at closure. The second part of CA1, the re-evaluation of the augmented designs on all runs, is carried by the Version 2.0 reports of the two steps, due on `{python} capa.loc["CA1", "due"]`, together with the models chosen by model selection. Both were open at closure.

Preventive action PA1, the sample-size calculation for each new characterization plan, checks each new design by simulation before its plan is approved, at the expected effects and with the analysis the plan states. The simulation of @sec-sample-size used the full quadratic model, the analysis the Version 1.0 plans prescribed. Preventive action PA2 revises SOP-1002, the procedure for the `{python} sop1002`, so that a plan states its model-selection procedure.

# Effectiveness check {#sec-effectiveness}

The actions are checked for effectiveness by `{python} EFFECTIVENESS2["due"]`. The check is recorded in three parts:

1. `{python} eff_items[0]`
2. `{python} eff_items[1]`
3. `{python} eff_items[2]`

The second part tests the prediction of new runs. Under a correct model each confirmation run falls inside its 95 % prediction interval with a probability of `{python} f2(cover)`, and the number inside follows a binomial distribution. The test rejects the model when that number is so low that a correct model would give it with a probability below `{python} f"{eff_alpha:g}"`. With `{python} eff_n` confirmation runs at least `{python} binom_min(eff_n)` must fall inside, and with `{python} eff_n2` at least `{python} binom_min(eff_n2)`. In the second part, a selected model meets the model-adequacy criteria of the process characterization master plan (PCMP-001 §7.2) when it shows `{python} TESTS`. Applied to the augmentation runs of this investigation, the binomial test rejects the models of high mannose and aggregates at the production bioreactor that were selected on the planned runs (@sec-sel-aug).

# Conclusion and closure {#sec-closure}

The investigation confirmed the classification as `{python} INV2["classification"]`, on the grounds recorded when it was opened (`{python} class_basis`). No range was set from a failing model at Version 2.0.

The root cause is that the plans prescribed the full quadratic model as the predictive model, with no model selection, on designs that are small for it. The Version 1.0 plans set no adequacy criterion against which the size of a design could have been checked. A remedy was assigned to every failing model by a rule approved before any new run, and both augmentations were run by `{python} last_end`. Model selection then replaced the refits for every output. Once selected, the models that the augmentations were made for meet the model-adequacy criteria (`{python} TESTS`) on the planned runs alone. On all runs the full quadratic model with a block term, which the augmentations were sized for, meets the lack-of-fit test and the limit on overfitting for `{python} join_and(attr_prose(r, k) for k, r in (AV, HCP))`, and not for `{python} attr_prose(HM[1], HM[0])`. The models of high mannose and aggregates at the production bioreactor, selected on the planned runs, predicted fewer of the new runs within their intervals than a binomial test allows, and the reports use the models of all runs. After selection `{python} n_none_sel` outputs have no adequate model, and every measured result of these outputs meets its criterion.

The intermediate acceptance criteria in force were fixed on the selected models at the closure of the investigation into acceptance criteria set after the data were seen (INV-001). Against the criteria that the full quadratic models give, model selection made `{python} n_wider` intermediate acceptance criteria wider and kept the upper limit of acidic variants at the production bioreactor at its a priori value. No conclusion over the NOR depends on that difference, and one proven acceptable range moves at its lower end, outside the NOR. The qualification of the scale-down model for host cell protein in the Protein A pool and at cation exchange does depend on it. The augmentation runs moved no criterion.

At closure the augmentation runs of corrective action CA1 and the refits of corrective action CA2 were complete. The re-evaluation on all runs of CA1 and the application of model selection, corrective action CA3, in the Version 2.0 reports were open, due on `{python} capa.loc["CA3", "due"]`. The preventive actions were open. INV-002 was closed on `{python} INV2["closed"]`.
